stops.title: Why this paper
stops.text: Before we open LFM2, let me tell you what it assumes. This report from Liquid AI is about speed on ordinary hardware. The authors rebuild the language model so it runs fast on a phone or laptop processor, then reuse it for an image model and a speech model. For your assignment, these are some of the smallest image and speech models in the atlas, which makes them good candidates for a free Colab GPU.

stops.title: What a layer remembers
stops.text: First idea. A model reads your prompt in one parallel pass, called prefill, and then writes one token at a time, called decode. An attention layer keeps a key and a value for every earlier token. That store is the KV cache, and it grows as the conversation grows. LFM2's short convolution only looks at the last two tokens, so its memory stays tiny. On a phone, that difference is speed.

stops.title: Speech in, codes out
stops.text: Second idea, for the audio model. Listening and speaking work differently. Incoming sound becomes a log-mel spectrogram, a picture of energy per frequency over time, and an encoder turns it into one vector every eighty milliseconds. Speaking goes the other way: the model predicts eight codes of the Mimi audio codec for each frame, and a small decoder turns those codes back into sound. The distillation panel beside the first one explains how the text model learned from a bigger teacher.

stops.title: Words to keep handy
stops.text: Keep this glossary open while you read. Four terms matter most. Word error rate is how speech recognition is scored, and lower is better. Grouped-query attention lets several heads share one cache. Mixture of experts means a large model that only uses a small part of itself for each token. And Q four zero is the four bit format used in the speed tests.

stops.title: Where LFM2 sits
stops.text: Finally, the map. Before this, Voxtral Realtime made speech recognition live. LFM2 steps back to the backbone itself, and shows that one fast backbone can carry text, images and speech. But notice the catch: images and voice live in two separate models, so a spoken question about a photo needs a pipeline. Next, MiniMind-O puts all three into one tiny model. When you're ready, press Play guided tour.
